Hi Olivia / Finovo team — answers inline below. Apologies for the slightly longer note; wanted to be explicit.

1) Transient routing through US IP ranges
- Current behavior: telemetry is routed to the nearest edge collector, which may transit through regional egress points. However, when a customer requests EU-only residency we pin the telemetry shard to EU storage and configure regional routing so that no persistent egress lands in the US. Transient hops within CDN or transit providers can occur (BGP-level) but payloads are encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+), and we can add a contractual clause restricting intentional data export to non-EU regions except for emergency diagnostics with documented approvals.

2) Retention policy
- Default: 90 days for aggregated telemetry.
- Option: we can set Finovo to a 30-day retention window during onboarding (config flag). Any retention shorter than 90 days may affect some long-term regression analytics; we’ll document expected impacts in the onboarding notes.

3) SLA / no cross-border egress clause
- We can accept a contractual statement that no intentional cross-border egress will occur except for emergency with documented approvals. We’ll need legal to review the precise language (we propose an agreed escalation workflow + audit trail requirement). Cost/ops impact: minimal for configuration; legal review required (3–5 business days).

Attachments included in the DocuSign packet:
- edgemetrics-dpa-addendum.pdf (draft; names Edgemetrics as subprocessor and includes residency clause)
- edgemetrics-eu-dataflow-diagram.png (flow with pinned EU storage)
- edgemetrics-soc2-snapshot.pdf (redacted)

Next steps

- Kimberly will drop a short one-pager on controls and expected impacts for 30-day retention.
- Laura will prepare the onboarding checklist with timelines for switch-over (expected 48–72 hours to fully pin routing once config is applied).
